turns.content: An unknown belongs to a family of saturated acyclic carboxylic acids with two adjacent methine carbons, methyl or ethyl branches, and an acid group attached either directly or through CH2. Its FTIR has a broad band near 3000 cm^-1 and a strong band near 1700 cm^-1; its proton NMR has no vinyl signals but includes one dtq and one dtt resonance. What constraints do these observations impose?
Interpret the two IR bands and absence of vinyl protons, separating evidence for the functional class from evidence about branching topology.
Under a first-order splitting model, translate dtq and dtt into distinct neighboring proton-set sizes and state the assumptions behind that interpretation.
What arrangement of adjacent methines, methyl, ethyl, methylene, and carboxyl-bearing groups can produce both patterns in the same saturated acid?
Identify the unknown by its complete condensed structure and map each complex methine resonance to its neighboring proton sets.
How strongly does this limited one-dimensional evidence support the assignment under the first-order model?
Check the proposal against its carbon count, carboxylic-acid functionality, and both coupling patterns, noting the missing shifts, integrations, and 2D correlations.
Report the condensed structure with an appropriate confidence qualification.
